ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle A=108^\circ$, the perpendicular bisector of $AD$ intersects diagonal $BD$ at point $P$, with the foot of the perpendicular being $N$. Connecting $CP$, what is the measure of $\angle BPC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect AP, \\
in the rhombus ABCD, where $\angle ADC=72^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADP = \frac{1}{2} \angle ADC = \frac{1}{2} \times 72^\circ = 36^\circ$, \\
$\because$ NP is the perpendicular bisector of AB, \\
$\therefore AP = CP$, \\
$\therefore \angle ADP = \angle DAP = 36^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle APB = \angle ADP + \angle DAP = 36^\circ + 36^\circ = 72^\circ$, \\
Due to the symmetry of the rhombus, $\angle CPB = \angle APB = 72^\circ$. \\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{72^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle A=108^\circ$. The perpendicular bisector of $AD$ intersects diagonal $BD$ at point $P$, and the foot of the perpendicular is $N$. Connect $CP$. What is the measure of $\angle BPC$ in degrees?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a rhombus ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, and D is at the upper left; diagonal BD has been drawn, point P is located on diagonal BD; point N is located on side AD, segment NP connects from N to P, and in combination with the meaning of the problem it is part of the perpendicular bisector of AD; segment CP has also been connected. Then reason: Because ABCD is a rhombus, and ∠A=108°, adjacent interior angles are supplementary, giving ∠B=∠D=180°−108°=72°. The diagonal BD of a rhombus bisects ∠B and ∠D, therefore ∠ADP=36°, and ∠PBC=36°. Also because P is on the perpendicular bisector of AD, PA=PD. Thus triangle APD is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠DAP=∠ADP=36°. Therefore ∠PAB=∠DAB−∠DAP=108°−36°=72°. In triangle ABP, ∠ABP=36°, ∠PAB=72°, so ∠APB=180°−36°−72°=72°. Thus ∠PAB=∠APB, obtaining AB=BP. In the rhombus AB=BC, so BP=BC. Therefore triangle BPC is an isosceles triangle, and the vertex angle ∠PBC=36°, therefore the two base angles are equal, ∠BPC=(180°−36°)/2=72°. Final answer: 72°.
